A very quiet doldrum-like pattern is expected in the wake of Typhoon
Sinlaku as it pulls further away from the northern CNMI. Light to 
gentle southwest to west winds will slowly shift toward the east- 
northeast early this coming week as trade winds become dominant, and
start to pick up toward the end of the week. In the meantime, light 
and variable winds are expected to develop for Guam and Rota tonight,
then Tinian and Saipan Sunday night behind the departing TY Sinlaku.
If there is enough clearing in the upper-level cloud deck and low- 
level moisture is sufficient, this may allow for afternoon island- 
effect showers to develop over Guam on Sunday. However, the current 
forecast indicates precipitable water amounts ranging 1.10 to 1.70 
inches which is fairly dry for the tropics.

Marine/Surf...
Typhoon Sinlaku continues to move northward and away from the 
northern CNMI, and marine conditions will gradually ease into 
early next week. The Hazardous Seas Warning was allowed to expire
this afternoon for Tinian and Saipan, but sea conditions will remain
elevated and hazardous to small craft through at least Sunday
afternoon. Buoy and altimetry data indicate combined seas are around
9 to 12 ft for Guam and Rota, and 10 to 14 feet for Tinian and 
Saipan as Sinlaku moves farther away from the northern CNMI. Light to
moderate southwest to west winds will continue through Sunday night,
gradually shifting to the east-northeast in the first half of the 
coming week as trade winds become dominant once more. Surf is also 
expected to slowly subside through the next few days as seas and 
swells diminish. Hazardous surf and dangerous rip currents are 
expected through late Sunday night along south, west, and north 
facing reefs, with the highest surf expected along north and west 
reefs. Minor coastal inundation of 1 to 2 feet is expected to 
continue at Tinian and Saipan through Sunday morning.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Sinlaku is located roughly near 23.3N 146.8E, or about 285 
miles north-northeast of Agrihan and 655 miles north of Guam, with 
the center moving northward, heading roughly toward the halfway point
between Iwo To and Minamitorishima. Maximum sustained winds remain 
near 75 mph as the storm persists just within low-end Category 1 
typhoon strength. The northeast periphery of Sinlaku is beginning to 
interact with a weak, trailing cold front which extends from a mid- 
latitude low-pressure system far to the northeast. The eye has filled
in and become difficult to distinguish, with the low- level 
circulation center becoming decoupled from the mid-levels. Outer 
rainbands extend roughly 600 miles west of the center and 400 miles 
outward to the north, east, and south. The Typhoon Warning for 
Agrihan in the CNMI was cancelled this morning as Sinlaku moved away,
and the last local statement was issued shortly after. The latest 
forecast from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) shows TY 
Sinlaku falling below typhoon strength early this evening, then 
exiting Guam's Area of Responsibility (AOR) north of 25N early Sunday
morning as it begins extratropical transition.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
There are two weather makers in the region. The first is a 
convergence zone in southern Pohnpei State. The other is the 
Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) with embedded troughs.

The convergence zone is producing widespread showers and isolated
thunderstorms around the islands of Sapwuafik, Nukuoro and
Kapingamarangi. These showers are expected to move westward over the
next day or two. 

The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is extending across the
Date Line to around 3N165E. Showers have spread from the ITCZ axis
about 325 miles north and about 225 miles to the south or from the
equator to about 8N. This feature is expected to continue building
westward. This expected to bring mostly scattered with a few pockets
of widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms to Kosrae, Majuro, 
Ailinglaplap, Jaluit, Namorik just to name a few. Model guidance 
suggests the ITCZ is anticipated to bring showers through Monday for 
Majuro, Wednesday for Kosrae, and most of next week for Pohnpei.

Altimetry shows combined seas of 5 to 6 feet throughout eastern 
Micronesia. ASCAT shows light to gentle winds with a few pockets of 
moderate speeds. Overall benign seas are expected through most of 
next week.

Western Micronesia...
A quiet weather pattern continues across the region this afternoon.
Drier air amongst light to gentle north-northwest winds is
suppressing shower potentials across Yap and Palau. Light afternoon
winds on Sunday and Monday may support island-effect showers,
however, there is some uncertainty in this due to the limited 
atmospheric moisture available. Overall, isolated light showers are
